items.title: Arrival — Montevideo
items.pace: Land at Carrasco, transfer in, keep the evening light
items.tldr: Land at Carrasco, settle into Ciudad Vieja or Pocitos, and ease in with an early dinner.
items.body:
No nonstop flight covers JFK–MVD, so plan on arriving tired from a connection. Clear immigration (visa-free for a US passport, up to 90 days), then take the airport taxi or bus into town — both are described in the Transit tab.

Keep the first evening unambitious: a walk along the Rambla near your hotel, or an early dinner at Mercado del Puerto (El Palenque is open Fridays 12:00–23:00) if the flight lands with enough daylight left.
constraints: Confirm your connection buffer before booking — every JFK–MVD routing has a stop

items.title: Day trip — Colonia del Sacramento
items.pace: Early bus out, full day in the old town, evening bus back
items.tldr: A full day in Uruguay's UNESCO river town — cobblestones, the lighthouse, sunset over the Río de la Plata.
items.body:
Take an early COT bus from Tres Cruces (≈2h20m) to Colonia del Sacramento's Barrio Histórico, a compact 17th–19th-century quarter that earned UNESCO World Heritage status in 1995 for its fused Portuguese-Spanish street plan.

Climb the Faro de Colonia (the 1857 lighthouse built over the ruined San Francisco convent) for a rooftop view over the old town and the river toward Argentina — it's open Saturdays 10:00–12:00 and 15:00–17:00, {{fact:faro-colonia-35-uyu}}, closed-toe shoes required. Wander the Calle de los Suspiros and the old port gate, then catch an evening bus back to Montevideo.
constraints: Faro de Colonia is open Thu–Sun only — this day (and Sun Feb 7) is the window for it

items.title: Ciudad Vieja & Carnival's home museum
items.pace: Morning walking tour, Mercado del Puerto lunch, museum in the afternoon
items.tldr: Montevideo's old town on foot — Palacio Salvo, a parrilla lunch at Mercado del Puerto, then the Carnival museum.
items.body:
Walk Ciudad Vieja starting at Plaza Independencia. Tour Palacio Salvo (Sunday slots run late morning and midafternoon, ≈45 min, tickets via Red Ticket only — ⚠ confirm the exact time at booking, sources disagree on the precise grid) for its Art Deco lobby, tango museum, and rooftop viewpoint over the city.

Have lunch at Mercado del Puerto — the 1868 iron-frame market hall itself is worth seeing, and El Palenque is open Sundays 12:00–17:00. In the afternoon, visit the Museo del Carnaval (Wed–Sun 11:00–17:00, {{fact:museo-carnaval-200-uyu}}) on the Rambla near the port — the closest thing to an official primer on the world's longest Carnival, useful groundwork before the holiday days ahead.
constraints: Palacio Salvo tickets are Red Ticket only — buy ahead, not at the door
Museo del Carnaval is closed Mondays and Tuesdays

items.title: Bodega Bouza & the Carnival holiday
items.pace: Winery morning, relaxed afternoon — many museums are shut for the holiday
items.tldr: A wine-country morning at Bodega Bouza, then a slow afternoon while Montevideo runs its Carnival-holiday hours.
items.body:
Feb 8 is one of Uruguay's two Carnival public holidays (the dates are fixed relative to Easter, not separately announced each year) — expect government offices and some museums to close or run short hours, even though it's a normal working day by law for private business.

Spend the morning at Bodega Bouza in Melilla (≈15 min by taxi from downtown), a boutique winery known for Tannat, with a guided walk through the vineyard and a tasting or lunch. ⚠ Confirm Bouza's Monday hours directly before you go — sourcing for this pass could only confirm the winery's daily 11:00–18:00 opening in general, not a guaranteed Monday tour slot.
constraints: Carnival public holiday — confirm any museum's hours before counting on it today

items.title: Travel day — on to Punta del Este
items.pace: Late-morning bus, afternoon at the beach
items.tldr: Uruguay's second Carnival holiday doubles as the travel day east to Punta del Este.
items.body: Feb 9 is the second Carnival public holiday — a fitting day to be in transit rather than counting on things being open. Take the COT bus from Tres Cruces to Punta del Este (≈2h), check into your lodging, and spend the afternoon at Playa Mansa (calm, bay-facing) or Playa Brava (open ocean, the one with La Mano sculpture) to reset.

items.title: Punta del Este & Isla de Lobos
items.pace: Town in the morning, boat excursion at midday
items.tldr: La Mano, the harbor, and an afternoon boat out to South America's largest sea lion colony.
items.body: Walk the peninsula from the harbor to Playa Brava, past La Mano de Punta del Este (the half-buried hand sculpture) and the yacht marina. At midday, join the Isla de Lobos boat excursion (daily 12:00, ≈2h round trip, {{fact:isla-lobos-70-usd}}) — the island holds South America's largest sea lion colony and is closed to landing, so this is a boat-side view.

plan_b.body: If rough seas cancel the Isla de Lobos sailing, Casapueblo (Punta Ballena, open daily from 10:00) makes a same-region backup — move Thursday's plan up a day and push La Barra to the afternoon instead.

constraints: Isla de Lobos sails weather-permitting — no landing on the island itself

items.title: Casapueblo & La Barra
items.pace: Punta Ballena in the morning, La Barra in the afternoon, sunset at Casapueblo
items.tldr: Carlos Páez Vilaró's whitewashed cliffside house-museum, then La Barra's beach and bridge.
items.body:
Casapueblo, the artist Carlos Páez Vilaró's sprawling whitewashed compound on Punta Ballena (≈15 km from Punta del Este), is open daily from 10:00 ({{fact:casapueblo-entrance-uyu}}) and is one of the few places on this coast with a genuinely well-known sunset. Time the visit for late afternoon.

On the way, stop in La Barra — the drawbridge, the boutique strip, and Playa Montoya are a quieter, younger-skewing alternative to central Punta del Este's beaches.

items.title: Beach day, with an optional detour
items.pace: Slow beach day — or an early start for Cabo Polonio
items.tldr: A deliberately unstructured beach day, with Cabo Polonio's wild sea lion coast as a big-commitment alternative.
items.body:
Keep this day open — a beach afternoon at Playa Mansa or a slower José Ignacio-area stretch, with no fixed plan.

For a more ambitious nature day, Cabo Polonio (a dune-and-lighthouse settlement with its own wild sea lion colony) is reachable from this coast, but it's a real undertaking: roughly 1.5 hours by road plus a 4x4 transfer across the dunes each way, effectively consuming the whole day. Worth the detour for a nature-first traveler; not a fit if the priority is rest before departure.

items.title: Return & departure
items.pace: Morning bus back to Montevideo, buffer for the flight
items.tldr: Bus back to Montevideo with a wide buffer, then the international flight home.
items.body: Take a mid-morning COT bus from Punta del Este back to Montevideo (≈2h) — build in a wide buffer given a connecting international itinerary, and confirm your outbound routing's check-in window before finalizing the bus time.
